title: Treasure Beneath the Sand
bigQuestion: How can we explore the past?

lingo.name: Lingo
lingo.persona: warm, playful owl teacher who loves history and asks lots of questions

mia.name: Mia
mia.persona: curious 11-year-old girl, excited and brave, speaks quickly when she is thrilled

leo.name: Leo
leo.persona: friendly 11-year-old boy, funny and careful, likes to double-check things

ruth.name: Ms Ruth
ruth.persona: calm, warm museum guide, encouraging and clear, speaks slowly

focusWords.kidDefinition: A collection of valuable things, like gold and jewels.
examples: The pirates hid their treasure in a dark cave.
Divers found a treasure of old gold coins under the sea.
focusWords.greekHint: θησαυρός: think of a 'thesauros' chest full of gold.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To move earth with your hands or a spade.
examples: Children love to dig in the sand at the beach.
Farmers dig holes to plant new trees every spring.
focusWords.greekHint: σκάβω: dig a hole and say 'σκάβω' as you dig.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A precious stone, often used in jewellery.
examples: She wore a ring with a bright blue jewel.
The king's crown was covered with jewels.
focusWords.greekHint: πετράδι: a stone that sparkles like a diamond.

focusWords.kidDefinition: Hidden under the ground or sand.
examples: My grandfather found a coin buried in his garden.
The old letters were buried in a box under the bed.
focusWords.greekHint: θαμμένος: something that is 'θαμμένος' is under the earth.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A person who sails the sea and steals things.
examples: The pirate wore a hat and carried a map.
Long ago, pirates sailed across the seas looking for gold.
focusWords.greekHint: πειρατής: think of a pirate ship with a black flag.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A hard hat that protects your head.
examples: Builders wear a yellow helmet to keep their heads safe.
The soldier's bronze helmet is on display in the museum.
focusWords.greekHint: κράνος: a helmet keeps the head safe, like a κράνος.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A ship that has been destroyed at sea.
examples: Divers explored the shipwreck at the bottom of the bay.
A storm caused the shipwreck near the rocky coast.
focusWords.greekHint: ναυάγιο: a ship that is broken in the sea.

examples: The stone will sink if you drop it in the pool.
The old boat sank during the storm last winter.
focusWords.greekHint: βυθίζομαι: sink goes down, like a βύθος (deep sea).

focusWords.kidDefinition: Soil, the brown earth on the ground.
examples: Plants grow well in dark, rich dirt.
Wash your hands after you play in the dirt.
focusWords.greekHint: χώμα: brown dirt that you can feel in your hands.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A place where a dead person is buried.
examples: Explorers opened the old tomb very carefully.
Inside the tomb, they found pots and golden masks.
focusWords.greekHint: τάφος: a tomb is a τάφος, a place for very old treasures.

lines.text: Hello, explorers! I am Lingo, and I love learning about the past.
Long ago, people hid gold, coins and jewels in secret places.
Today, archaeologists still find amazing things under the ground.
Some treasures were lost at sea, and some were buried in old tombs.

question.text: If you found an old box under the sand, what would you hope was inside?

caption.text: One sunny morning, Mia and Leo found a dusty paper on the beach.

speech.text: Look, Mia! It is an old map, and it shows a treasure!
I think the treasure is buried near that big rock.

caption.text: They ran to the rock and started to dig.

speech.text: Let's dig here! A pirate probably hid it long ago.
Good idea. Please pass me the spade.

caption.text: Mia dug and dug, until her spade hit something hard.

speech.text: Wait! I can see a shiny jewel in the dirt!
Wow, let's keep going carefully, so we do not break it.

caption.text: Leo brushed away the sand and found an old helmet.

speech.text: Look, a rusty helmet! It must come from a shipwreck.
The ship probably sank long ago, near these rocks.

caption.text: A week later, Ms Ruth showed them a picture of an ancient tomb.

speech.text: This tomb is thousands of years old. You two are real explorers!
Next time, we will look for another tomb!

prompt.text: Listen to the word and choose the picture: treasure.

explain.text: A treasure is a collection of valuable things, like gold and jewels.

prompt.text: Which picture shows a sparkling stone you could wear in a ring?

explain.text: A jewel is a precious stone, and it sparkles in the sun.

prompt.text: Archaeologists ____ carefully to find old coins.

explain.text: Dig means to move earth with a spade or your hands.

prompt.text: Something that is buried is hidden under the ground.

explain.text: Buried means that something is covered and hidden, like sand over a box.

prompt.text: The ____ hid gold coins on a secret island long ago.

explain.text: A pirate is a person who sails the sea and steals things.

prompt.text: Which word is the odd one out?

explain.text: Sink is a verb, but the others are nouns you can hold.

prompt.text: Which picture shows the brown earth you dig through?

explain.text: Dirt is the soil on the ground, and plants grow in it.

prompt.text: The ancient king rested in a stone ____ for thousands of years.

explain.text: A tomb is a place where a dead person is buried.

prompt.text: A shipwreck is a new ship that is still sailing across the sea.

explain.text: A shipwreck is a ship that has been destroyed at sea, so it is not sailing.

prompt.text: Ancient soldiers wore a bronze ____ to protect their heads.

explain.text: A helmet is a hard hat that protects your head.

lines.text: Time to play memory! Find two cards that match: a word and its picture.
Say each word out loud as you turn the card over.

prompt.text: With your partner, imagine you are explorers on a beach. Use the frames to say what you might find.

frames: I think a ___ is buried under the sand.
I found a ___ in the dirt!

model.text: I think a treasure is buried under the sand. I would dig here because the map shows a big rock. I found a jewel in the dirt!

lines.text: Brilliant work, explorers! You dug up ten new words today.
Next time, we will find out how archaeologists explore the past.

exitTicket.text: Which word means a hard hat that protects your head?
Write one sentence using the word buried.
